doc.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021

title: Israel as home and the pandemic spent in Rio
summary: Israel is home; she describes Tel Aviv and says the Tiny Desk concert was filmed in Rio during the pandemic.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: I would imagine like all other musicians and most people, you had a challenge during this Covid pandemic as far as gigs. Did you stay in the States or did you go home, or do you still think of Israel as home? © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

Yeah, Israel will always be home, there’s where I grew up, that’s where my mom and my siblings are, and I love it. I just spent one month there and it was incredible. I love Tel Aviv, my city. I love driving around on my scooter and I love being able to stop and go into the city, the city is right on the beach and it’s a lovely city. Complex place but a lovely, lovely city. But when the pandemic started I went down to Rio De Janeiro, and I thought it was just for a little bit. And I stayed there for a while. So the “Tiny Desk” concert you saw was filmed in Rio De Janeiro, it was filmed during the pandemic.
